title: Comparison and gluing of regular loci on affine charts
statement: Let $Y$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and put $\operatorname{Reg}(Y)=\{z\in Y:\mathcal O_{Y,z}\text{ is a regular local ring}\}$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For a commutative ring $C$ put $E(C)=\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}C:C_{\mathfrak q}\text{ is a regular local ring}\}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. For every affine open $W\subseteq Y$, with $C=\mathcal O_Y(W)$, the canonical homeomorphism $\alpha_W:W\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}C$ satisfies $W\cap\operatorname{Reg}(Y)=\alpha_W^{-1}(E(C))$. Consequently, for every affine open covering $Y=\bigcup_{j\in J}W_j$, the set $\operatorname{Reg}(Y)$ is open in $Y$ if and only if every $E(\mathcal O_Y(W_j))$ is open in its prime spectrum. In particular, for a Noetherian commutative ring $B$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$, under the canonical identification of its points with primes of $B$, $\operatorname{Reg}(Y)=E(B)$ and their openness is equivalent. Empty schemes and infinite coverings are allowed.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $W\subseteq Y$ and $z\in W$, and write $C=\mathcal O_Y(W)$ and $\mathfrak q=\alpha_W(z)$. The canonical immersion $\iota_W:\operatorname{Spec}C\to Y$ in the affine-stalk theorem restricts to the inverse of the canonical chart $\alpha_W$, so $\iota_W(\mathfrak q)=z$. Thus the prime $\mathfrak p_z$ of that theorem is exactly $\mathfrak q$, and its clause (c) gives a ring isomorphism $C_{\mathfrak q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{Y,z}$. Apply ring-isomorphism invariance to this isomorphism and its inverse: $C_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local if and only if $\mathcal O_{Y,z}$ is regular local. By the definitions of $E(C)$ and $\operatorname{Reg}(Y)$ this is exactly $z\in\alpha_W^{-1}(E(C))$ if and only if $z\in W\cap\operatorname{Reg}(Y)$. Equality of these subsets follows pointwise.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), part (6), on an affine open; algebra.tex, Tag 00KU (definition-regular-local).

proof.text: Put $T=\operatorname{Reg}(Y)$. If $T$ is open, then $T\cap W_j$ is open in $W_j$; its image under the homeomorphism $\alpha_{W_j}$ is $E(\mathcal O_Y(W_j))$, hence is open. Conversely, if all these ring loci are open, their inverse images under $\alpha_{W_j}$ are open in $W_j$. Each $W_j$ is open in $Y$, so these subsets are also open in $Y$: a subset open in the subspace $W_j$ is $W_j\cap O$ for an ambient open $O$. Since the $W_j$ cover $Y$, $T=\bigcup_j(T\cap W_j)$; arbitrary unions of opens are open. These statements follow from the definitions of a homeomorphism, the subspace topology and a topology; no finiteness of the covering is used.

source.place: Tag 07R4 (lemma-J), proof, last paragraph, openness from the affine covering.

proof.text: For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$, its underlying topological space is the prime spectrum of $B$ and its global sections identify canonically with $B$. Applying the affine-stalk localization theorem on the whole affine scheme therefore gives $\mathcal O_{Y,\mathfrak p}\cong B_{\mathfrak p}$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $B$. Ring-isomorphism invariance in both directions identifies membership in $\operatorname{Reg}(Y)$ with membership in $E(B)$. These are equal subsets of the same prime spectrum, so their openness is equivalent. If $B$ is the zero ring, both spectra and both loci are empty. For an empty $Y$ the pointwise comparison is vacuous and the union in the preceding step is empty, including for an empty covering.
